title.zh: 卷一百二十六 列傳第七十六: 李揆 李涵 陳少游 盧鸑 裴諝
title.en: Volume 126 Biographies 76: Li Kui, Li Han, Chen Shaoyou, Lu Yue, Pei Xu
title.raw: 卷一百二十六 列傳第七十六: 李揆 李涵 陳少游 盧鸑 裴諝 Volume 126 Biographies 76: Li Kui, Li Han, Chen Shaoyou, Lu Yue, Pei Xu

sentences.zh: 李揆字端卿，隴西成紀人，而家於鄭州，代為冠族。

translations.literal: Li Kui, courtesy name Duanqing, was a native of Chengji in Longxi, but his family had settled in Zhengzhou, and for generations they were a leading clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui, whose courtesy name was Duanqing, came from Chengji in Longxi, though his family had long lived in Zhengzhou and ranked among the foremost lineages of the age.

sentences.zh: 秦府學士、給事中玄道玄孫，秘書監、贈吏部尚書成裕之子。

translations.literal: He was the great-great-grandson of Xuantao, academician of the Prince of Qin's establishment and supervising censor, and the son of Chengyu, director of the Secretariat, posthumously honored as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was descended from Xuantao, who had served as an academician in the Prince of Qin's household and as a supervising censor, and was the son of Chengyu, director of the Secretariat, who after death was posthumously honored as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and fond of study, and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was quick-witted and devoted to learning, and showed a gift for writing.

sentences.zh: 開元末，舉進士，補陳留尉，獻書闕下，詔中書試文章，擢拜右拾遺。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed assistant magistrate of Chenliu, presented a book at the palace gates, and by imperial order the Secretariat tested his writings; he was then promoted and appointed Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Near the close of the Kaiyuan reign he took the jinshi degree, served as assistant magistrate of Chenliu, and submitted a work to the court. The emperor ordered the Secretariat to examine his prose, after which he was elevated to Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 改右補闕、起居郎，知宗子表疏。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Supplementation Censor and Imperial Diarist, and was charged with imperial-clan memorials and reports.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made Right Supplementation Censor and Imperial Diarist, with responsibility for memorials from members of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 遷司勛員外郎、考功郎中，並知制誥。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director in the Bureau of Merits and to director in the Bureau of Evaluations, and in both posts he drafted imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director in the Bureau of Merits and director in the Bureau of Evaluations, holding in each office the duty of drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 扈從劍南，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: When he followed the emperor to Jiannan, he was appointed Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying the court into Jiannan, he was appointed drafting secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，兼禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyuan era he also served as vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianyuan era he was given the additional post of vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 揆嘗以主司取士，多不考實，徒峻其堤防，索其書策，殊未知藝不至者，文史之囿亦不能摛詞，深昧求賢之意也。

translations.literal: Kui once remarked that chief examiners in selecting scholars often did not verify substance, but merely heightened barriers, demanding written answers, utterly failing to see that when talent falls short one cannot even compose within the bounds of letters and histories, deeply betraying the intent of seeking the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Kui had observed that those who presided over examinations often tested candidates on form alone, raising barriers and demanding written responses without recognizing that men lacking real ability could not even frame an argument within the literary canon—thus missing entirely the purpose of seeking talent.

sentences.zh: 其試進士文章，請於庭中設《五經》、諸史及《切韻》本於床，而引貢士謂之曰：「大國選士，但務得者，經籍在此，請恣尋檢。」

translations.literal: For the jinshi literary examination he had copies of the Five Classics, the various histories, and the Qieyun placed on tables in the courtyard, and addressing the candidates said: "A great state selects scholars and cares only to obtain the capable; the classics are here—please search them freely."
translations.idiomatic: When he tested jinshi candidates on their essays, he had copies of the Five Classics, the standard histories, and the Qieyun set out on tables in the courtyard and told the examinees: "Our realm seeks men of talent, not memorizers. The texts are here—use them as you will."

sentences.zh: 由是數月之間，美聲上聞，未及畢事，遷中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿崇文館大學士、修國史。

translations.literal: From this, within a few months his fine reputation reached the throne; before the examinations were finished he was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat, made a chief minister, grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and the Chongwen Pavilion, and charged with compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Within months his reputation reached the emperor. Before the examination season ended he was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, appointed chief minister, made grand academician of the imperial libraries, and assigned to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 揆美風儀，善奏對，每有敷陳，皆符獻替。

translations.literal: Kui had a fine bearing and was skilled in memorial responses; whenever he presented counsel it accorded with the principle of offering and replacing.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was distinguished in bearing and eloquent in audience. Each proposal he offered struck the mark of sound counsel.

sentences.zh: 肅宗賞嘆之，嘗謂揆曰：「卿門地、人物、文章，皆當代所推。」

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong admired him and once said to Kui: "Your lineage, your person, and your writings are all praised in this age."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong admired him greatly and once told him: "Your family standing, your character, and your prose are alike the finest of our day."

sentences.zh: 故進人稱為三絕。

translations.literal: Hence contemporaries called these the three excellences.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time therefore spoke of his "three unrivaled gifts."

sentences.zh: 其為舍人也，宗室請加張皇后「翊聖」之號，肅宗召揆問之，對曰；

translations.literal: When he was a drafting secretary, members of the imperial clan asked that the title "Assisting Sage" be added for Empress Zhang. Emperor Suzong summoned Kui to inquire, and he replied:
translations.idiomatic: While he was still a drafting secretary, the imperial clan petitioned to add the honorific "Assisting Sage" to Empress Zhang's title. Suzong called Kui in for his view, and he answered:

sentences.zh: 「臣觀往古后妃，終則有謚。

translations.literal: "Your servant observes that empresses and consorts of old received posthumous titles only at the end.
translations.idiomatic: "In antiquity, empresses and consorts received posthumous titles only after death.

sentences.zh: 生加尊號，未之前聞。

translations.literal: To add an honorific title during life has never been heard of before.
translations.idiomatic: To bestow such an honorific upon a living empress was without precedent.

sentences.zh: 景龍失政，韋氏專恣，加號翊聖，今若加皇后之號，與韋氏同。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era government failed, the Wei clan acted willfully, and the title Assisting Sage was added; if the empress is given this title now, it will be the same as with the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Under the misrule of the Jinglong years Empress Wei had seized power and taken the title Assisting Sage. To grant the same title now would repeat that unhappy precedent.

sentences.zh: 陛下明聖，動遵典禮，豈可蹤景龍故事哉！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is enlightened and sage, and in every act follows the canonical rites—how could you follow the Jinglong precedent!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is enlightened and devoted to ritual. How could you follow the example of the Jinglong era!"

sentences.zh: 肅宗驚曰：「凡才幾誤我家事。」

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong said in alarm: "Mediocre talent nearly ruined my household affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Suzong started in alarm. "Mediocre advisers nearly ruined my house," he said.

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: The matter was thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時代宗自廣平王改封成王，張皇后有子數歲，陰有奪宗之議。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Daizong had been changed from Prince of Guangping to Prince of Cheng; Empress Zhang had a son of several years, and secretly there was talk of displacing the heir.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Daizong, formerly Prince of Guangping, had been redesignated Prince of Cheng. Empress Zhang had a young son, and quietly there was talk of setting him up as heir instead.

sentences.zh: 揆因對見，肅宗從容曰：「成王嫡長有功，今當命嗣，卿意何如？」

translations.literal: When Kui next had an audience, Emperor Suzong said at ease: "The Prince of Cheng is the eldest legitimate son and has merit; he should now be named heir—what is your view?"
translations.idiomatic: On another audience Kui was present when Suzong said casually: "The Prince of Cheng is the eldest legitimate son and has earned distinction. It is time to name the heir. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 揆拜賀曰：「陛下言及於此，社稷之福，天下幸甚，臣不勝大慶。」

translations.literal: Kui bowed in congratulation and said: "When Your Majesty speaks to this point, it is the fortune of the altars of soil and grain; the realm is greatly blessed, and your servant cannot contain his great rejoicing."
translations.idiomatic: Kui bowed in congratulation. "When Your Majesty speaks thus, the altars of state are blessed and the realm rejoices. Your servant is overcome with joy."

sentences.zh: 肅宗喜曰：「朕計決矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong said with pleasure: "My decision is made."
translations.idiomatic: Suzong said with satisfaction: "My mind is made up."

sentences.zh: 自此頗承恩遇，遂蒙大用。

translations.literal: From this he received considerable imperial favor and soon came to great employment.
translations.idiomatic: From that time he enjoyed the emperor's favor and was soon entrusted with the highest responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 時京師多盜賊，有通衢殺人置溝中者，李輔國方恣橫，上請選羽林騎士五百人以備巡檢。

translations.literal: At the time the capital had many bandits; there were cases of men killed on thoroughfares and cast into ditches. Li Fuguo was then acting with unchecked power and petitioned to select five hundred Imperial Guard horsemen for patrol inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was rife in the capital; murder victims were left in the streets. Li Fuguo, then riding high, asked to assign five hundred Imperial Guard cavalry to patrol duty.

sentences.zh: 揆上疏曰：「昔西漢以南北軍相攝，故周勃因南軍入北軍，遂安劉氏。

translations.literal: Kui submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly in Western Han the Southern and Northern Armies kept each other in check; thus Zhou Bo entered the Northern Army through the Southern Army and thereby secured the Liu house.
translations.idiomatic: Kui memorialized: "In Western Han the Southern and Northern Armies were made to balance each other. That was how Zhou Bo, entering the Northern Army through the Southern, was able to save the Liu dynasty.

sentences.zh: 皇朝置南北衙，文武區分，以相伺察。

translations.literal: Our dynasty established the Southern and Northern Bureaus, separating civil and military, to watch each other.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty likewise divided civil and military authority between the Southern and Northern Bureaus so that each might keep watch upon the other.

sentences.zh: 今以羽林代金吾警夜，忽有非常之變，將何以制之？」

translations.literal: Now to replace the Gold Crow Guard with the Imperial Guard for night watch—if a sudden extraordinary change occurs, how will it be controlled?"
translations.idiomatic: If the Imperial Guard replaces the Gold Crow Guard on night patrol, who will restrain them should sudden trouble arise?"

sentences.zh: 遂制罷羽林之請。

translations.literal: An edict was thereupon issued stopping the request for the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accordingly rejected the request for Imperial Guard patrols.

sentences.zh: 揆在相位，決事獻替，雖甚博辨，性銳於名利，深為物議所非。

translations.literal: While Kui held the chief ministership he decided affairs with corrective counsel and was very broad in debate, but his nature was keen for fame and profit, and he was deeply criticized in public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister Kui was learned and forceful in debate, yet he was fiercely ambitious for rank and gain, and public opinion turned sharply against him.

sentences.zh: 又其兄皆自有時名，滯於冗官，竟不引進。

translations.literal: Moreover his elder brothers all had reputations in their own day but were stuck in superfluous posts; he never advanced them.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brothers, men of reputation in their own right, languished in minor posts, yet he never brought them forward.

sentences.zh: 同列呂諲，地望雖懸，政事在揆之右，罷相，自賓客為荊南節度，聲問甚美。

translations.literal: His colleague Lü Yin, though far beneath him in lineage and standing, had been above Kui in handling government; dismissed from the chief ministership, he went from guest minister to military commissioner of Jingnan, and his reputation was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: His colleague Lü Yin, though of far humbler birth, had once outranked him in power. After leaving the chief ministership Yin had served as guest minister and then as military commissioner of Jingnan, where his reputation flourished.

sentences.zh: 懼其重入，遂密令直省至諲管內抅求諲過失。

translations.literal: Fearing his return to office, Kui secretly ordered clerks of the Secretariat to go within Yin's jurisdiction and seek out Yin's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Yin's return to court, Kui secretly sent secretariat staff into his jurisdiction to dig up offenses.

sentences.zh: 諲密疏自陳，乃貶揆萊州長史同正員，其制旨曰：「扇湖南之八州，沮江陵之節制。」

translations.literal: Yin submitted a secret memorial in his own defense, and Kui was demoted to senior adjutant of Laizhou with the same nominal rank; the edict read: "He stirred the eight prefectures south of the lake and obstructed control at Jiangling."
translations.idiomatic: Yin lodged a secret defense of himself, and Kui was demoted to senior adjutant of Laizhou. The edict declared that he had "stirred unrest across the eight southern Hunan prefectures and obstructed military control at Jiangling."

sentences.zh: 揆既黜官，數日，其兄皆改授為司門員外郎。

translations.literal: After Kui was removed from office, within a few days his brothers were all reassigned as vice directors in the Bureau of Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Within days of Kui's dismissal his brothers were all appointed vice directors in the Bureau of Gates.

sentences.zh: 後累年，揆量移歙州刺史。

translations.literal: After several years Kui was transferred by seniority to prefect of Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he was transferred to the post of prefect of Shezhou.

sentences.zh: 初，揆秉政，侍中苗晉卿累薦元載為重官。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Kui held power, Chief Minister Miao Jinqing repeatedly recommended Yuan Zai for weighty office.
translations.idiomatic: While Kui was in power, Chief Minister Miao Jinqing had repeatedly recommended Yuan Zai for high office.

sentences.zh: 揆自恃門望，以載地寒，意甚輕易，不納，而謂晉卿曰：「龍章鳳姿之士不見用，麞頭鼠目之子乃求官。」

translations.literal: Kui relied on his own lineage prestige, regarded Zai as low in origin, treated him very lightly, and would not accept him, saying to Jinqing: "Men of dragon markings and phoenix bearing go unused, while sons with deer heads and rat eyes seek office."
translations.idiomatic: Trusting in his own pedigree, Kui looked down on Zai's humble origins and refused the recommendation, telling Jinqing: "Men of true distinction go unused while creatures with the heads of deer and the eyes of rats come begging for posts."

sentences.zh: 載銜恨頗深。

translations.literal: Zai bore a very deep grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Zai never forgave the insult.

sentences.zh: 及載登相位，因揆當徙職，遂奏為試秘書監，江淮養疾。

translations.literal: When Zai reached the chief ministership, taking advantage of Kui's due transfer of post, he memorialized that Kui be made acting director of the Secretariat to recuperate from illness in the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zai became chief minister and Kui was due for reassignment, he had him named acting director of the Secretariat and sent to convalesce in the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 既無祿俸，家復貧乏，孀孤百口，丐食取給。

translations.literal: He had no salary, his household was again impoverished, and a hundred mouths of widows and orphans begged for food to sustain themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Without salary and with his household in want, more than a hundred widows and orphans in his family lived by begging.

sentences.zh: 萍寄諸州，凡十五六年，其牧守稍薄，則又移居，故其遷徙者，蓋十余州焉。

translations.literal: He drifted like duckweed among the prefectures for altogether fifteen or sixteen years; whenever a prefect was somewhat cold to him he moved again, so that the places to which he shifted numbered more than ten prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: For fifteen or sixteen years he drifted from prefecture to prefecture. Whenever a local governor treated him coldly he moved on, passing through more than ten jurisdictions in all.

sentences.zh: 元載以罪誅，除揆睦州刺史，入拜國子祭酒、禮部尚書，為盧杞所惡。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zai was executed for crime, Kui was appointed prefect of Muzhou, entered the capital and was appointed chancellor of the National University and minister of rites, but was hated by Lu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Zai was executed for his crimes, Kui was made prefect of Muzhou, then recalled to serve as chancellor of the National University and minister of rites, but Lu Qi bore him ill will.

sentences.zh: 德宗在山南，令充入蕃會盟使，加左僕射。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong was in Shannan, Kui was ordered to serve as envoy to the Tibetans for the alliance conference, and was given the additional title of Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: While Dezong was in exile in Shannan, Kui was appointed envoy to Tibet for the peace conference and promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 行至鳳州，以疾卒，興元元年四月也，年七十四。

translations.literal: When he reached Fengzhou he died of illness, in the fourth month of the first year of Xingyuan, at the age of seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Fengzhou but died of illness there in the fourth month of the first year of Xingyuan, aged seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，喪事官給。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Grand Marshal and his funeral expenses were supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Marshal, and the state provided for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 李涵，高平王道立曾孫。

translations.literal: Li Han was the great-grandson of Li Daoli, Prince of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han was the great-grandson of Li Daoli, Prince of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 父少康，宋州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Shaokang was prefect of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaokang had served as prefect of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 涵簡素恭慎，有名宗室，累授贊善大夫、兼侍御史。

translations.literal: Han was plain, frugal, respectful, and cautious, a noted member of the imperial clan, and was repeatedly appointed gentleman attendant of the heir apparent and concurrently palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: Han was plain, modest, and careful in conduct, esteemed among the imperial clan, and rose through posts as gentleman attendant of the heir apparent and palace censor.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度郭子儀奏為關內鹽池判官。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi, military commissioner of Shuofang, memorialized that he be made salt-pond judge within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, military commissioner of Shuofang, recommended him as judge of the salt ponds within the passes.

sentences.zh: 肅宗北幸平涼，未有所適。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong went north to Pingliang he had not yet decided where to settle.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong fled north to Pingliang he had not yet chosen a destination.

sentences.zh: 涵與朔方留後杜鴻漸，草箋具朔方兵馬招集之勢，軍資倉儲庫物之數，鹹推涵宗枝之英，純厚忠信，乃令涵奉箋至平涼謁見。

translations.literal: Han and Du Hongjian, acting commissioner of Shuofang, drafted a memorial setting forth the strength of Shuofang troops being gathered, and the numbers of military supplies, granaries, and storehouse goods, all praising Han as an outstanding branch of the imperial clan, pure, thick, loyal, and trustworthy; Han was then ordered to present the memorial at Pingliang for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Du Hongjian, acting commissioner of Shuofang, drafted a memorial detailing the forces being mustered in Shuofang and the stores of grain, arms, and supplies on hand, praising Han as a worthy scion of the imperial house, steadfast and loyal. Han was sent to Pingliang to present it in person.

sentences.zh: 涵敷奏明辯，動合事機，肅宗大悅，除右司員外郎，累至司封郎中、宗正少卿。

translations.literal: Han presented his report clearly and persuasively, and his every motion suited the occasion; Emperor Suzong was greatly pleased and appointed him vice director in the Right Secretariat, then successively director in the Bureau of Enfeoffments and vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Han spoke with clarity and force, and his counsel matched the moment. Suzong was delighted and appointed him vice director in the Right Secretariat, then promoted him through the Bureau of Enfeoffments to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，初平河朔，代宗以涵忠謹洽聞，遷左庶子、兼御史中丞、河北宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, when Hebei was first pacified, Emperor Daizong, because Han was known for loyalty, prudence, and harmony, promoted him to left attendant of the heir apparent, concurrently censor-in-chief, and pacification commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying, as Hebei was brought back under control, Daizong, knowing Han for loyalty and steady judgment, made him left attendant of the heir apparent, censor-in-chief, and pacification commissioner for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 會丁母憂，起復本官而行，每州縣郵驛，公事之外，未嘗啟口，疏飯飲水，席地而息。

translations.literal: He happened to enter mourning for his mother, was recalled from mourning to his former office and set out; at every prefecture and county post station, apart from public business he never opened his mouth, ate plain rice and drank water, and slept on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was recalled from mourning to resume his post. At every relay station along the way he spoke only on official business, ate plain food, drank water, and slept on the ground.

sentences.zh: 使還，請罷官終喪制，代宗以其毀瘠，許之。

translations.literal: When the mission returned he asked to resign office and complete the mourning rites; Daizong, seeing how emaciated he was from grief, granted it.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he asked leave to complete the full mourning period. Daizong, seeing how grief had wasted him, consented.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除給事中，遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed supervising censor and promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was made supervising censor and then left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以幽州之亂，充河朔宣慰使。

translations.literal: Because of the turmoil in Youzhou he was made pacification commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble broke out in Youzhou he was again appointed pacification commissioner for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 大歷六年正月，為蘇州刺史、兼御史大夫，充浙江西道都團練觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year of Dali he became prefect of Suzhou, concurrently chief censor, and overall training-and-observation commissioner of the Western Zhejiang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year of Dali he was made prefect of Suzhou, chief censor, and overall military governor of Western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十一年，來朝，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he came to court and was appointed chief censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he came to court and was appointed chief censor.

sentences.zh: 京畿觀察使李棲筠歿，代之。

translations.literal: When Li Qiyun, observation commissioner of the capital region, died, Han replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Qiyun, observation commissioner of the capital region, died, Han succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，以涵和易，無剸割之才，除太子少傅，充山陵副使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, because Han was mild and easygoing and lacked the talent for decisive cutting, he was made junior tutor of the heir apparent and deputy commissioner for the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong came to the throne he judged Han too mild for hard decisions and made him junior tutor of the heir apparent and deputy commissioner for the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 涵判官殿中侍御史呂渭上言：「涵父名少康，今官名犯諱，恐乖禮典。」

translations.literal: Han's aide, palace censor Lü Wei, submitted a memorial saying: "Han's father's name is Shaokang; the present official title violates the taboo, and I fear this conflicts with ritual canon."
translations.idiomatic: Han's aide, palace censor Lü Wei, memorialized: "His father's name is Shaokang, yet his present title violates that taboo. This may offend ritual propriety."

sentences.zh: 宰相崔祐甫奏曰：「若朝廷事有乖舛，群臣悉能如此，實太平之道。」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Cui Youfu memorialized: "If whenever court affairs go astray all ministers can act thus, that is truly the way of great peace."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Cui Youfu replied: "If every minister spoke up whenever the court erred, that would be the way to true peace."

sentences.zh: 除渭司門員外郎。

translations.literal: Lü Wei was appointed vice director in the Bureau of Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wei was promoted to vice director in the Bureau of Gates.

sentences.zh: 尋有人言：「涵昔為宗正少卿，此時無言，今為少傅，妄有奏議。」

translations.literal: Soon someone said: "When Han was formerly vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan he said nothing; now that he is junior tutor he has allowed a reckless memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone objected: "When Han was vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, Lü Wei said nothing. Now that Han is junior tutor, this memorial is opportunistic."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「呂渭僭陳章奏，為其本使薄訴官名。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Lü Wei presumptuously submitted a memorial, making a petty complaint about an official title on behalf of his principal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Lü Wei overstepped his place by memorializing a petty complaint about his superior's title.

sentences.zh: 朕以宋有司城之嫌，晉有詞曹之諱，嘆其忠於所事，亦謂確以上聞。

translations.literal: We took the Song case of the taboo on Sicheng and the Jin taboo on Cicao, admired his loyalty to his charge, and also considered it a firm report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling how the Song avoided the name Sicheng and the Jin the name Cicao, We admired his loyalty to his superior and thought his report forthright.

sentences.zh: 乃加殊恩，俾膺厚賞。

translations.literal: We therefore granted him special favor and allowed him a rich reward.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore showed him special favor and a generous reward.

sentences.zh: 近聞所陳「少」字，往歲已任少卿，昔是今非，罔我何甚！

translations.literal: We have lately heard that the character shao he cited—years ago Han already held the post of vice director, what was right then is wrong now; how greatly he has deceived Us!
translations.idiomatic: We have since learned that the character shao he cited was no issue when Han already held the title of vice director. What was acceptable then is unacceptable now—how greatly he has deceived Us!

sentences.zh: 豈得謬當朝典，更廁周行，宜佐遐籓，用誡薄俗。

translations.literal: How can he wrongly occupy court canon and again take a place in the capital ranks? He should assist a distant frontier prefecture to admonish shallow custom.
translations.idiomatic: He cannot remain at court among the capital officials. Let him serve in a distant prefecture as a warning to shallow men.

sentences.zh: 可歙州司馬同正。」

translations.literal: He is fit to be secretary of Shezhou with the same nominal rank."
translations.idiomatic: He is demoted to secretary of Shezhou with nominal rank."

sentences.zh: 由是改涵為檢校工部尚書、兼光祿卿，仍充山陵副使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Han was changed to acting minister of works and concurrently director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, still serving as deputy commissioner for the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Han was reassigned as acting minister of works and director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, while retaining his post as deputy commissioner for the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 無幾，以右僕射致仕。

translations.literal: Before long he retired as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he retired with the title of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 興元元年九月卒，追贈太子太保。

translations.literal: He died in the ninth month of the first year of Xingyuan and was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of the first year of Xingyuan and was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 陳少遊，博州人也。

translations.literal: Chen Shaoyou was a man of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou was a native of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 祖儼，安西副都護。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan was vice protector-general of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan had served as vice protector-general of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 父慶，右武衛兵曹參軍，以少遊累贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Qing was a military staff officer of the Right Martial Guards; through Shaoyou's honors he was repeatedly posthumously honored as minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qing had been a staff officer in the Right Martial Guards and was posthumously honored as minister of works through Shaoyou's promotions.

sentences.zh: 少遊幼聰辯，初習《莊》、《列》、《老子》，為崇玄館學生，眾推引講經。

translations.literal: Shaoyou in youth was clever and eloquent; he first studied the Zhuangzi, Liezi, and Laozi, became a student of the Hall of Venerating Mystery, and the crowd pushed him forward to lecture on the classics.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Shaoyou was quick and articulate. He studied the Zhuangzi, Liezi, and Laozi, entered the Hall of Venerating Mystery as a student, and his fellows chose him to lecture on the classics.

sentences.zh: 時同列有私習經義者，期升坐日相問難。

translations.literal: At the time some of his fellows had privately studied the meaning of the classics and set a day when they would ascend the seat and question each other in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Some classmates had studied the classics on their own and arranged a day to take the lectern and challenge one another in debate.

sentences.zh: 及會，少遊攝齊升坐，音韻清辯，觀者屬目。

translations.literal: When they met, Shaoyou gathered his robes and ascended the seat; his tones were clear and his argument keen, and the onlookers fixed their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came, Shaoyou mounted the platform with measured step. His voice was clear and his reasoning sharp, and every eye in the hall was on him.

sentences.zh: 所引文句，悉兼他義，諸生不能對，甚為大學士陳希烈所嘆賞，又以同宗，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: The passages he cited all combined other meanings; the students could not reply, and Grand Academician Chen Xilie greatly admired him; moreover, being of the same clan, he treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Every passage he cited carried layered meanings his peers could not answer. Grand Academician Chen Xilie was deeply impressed and, finding they shared a clan name, treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 既擢第，補渝州南平令，理甚有聲。

translations.literal: After he passed the examination he was appointed magistrate of Nanping in Yuzhou, and his governance won great renown.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the examinations he was appointed magistrate of Nanping in Yuzhou, where his administration won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 至德中，河東節度王思禮奏為參謀，累授大理司直、監察殿中侍御史、節度判官。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era Wang Silu, military commissioner of Hedong, memorialized that he be made staff planner; he was repeatedly appointed rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review, investigating censor and palace censor, and military commissioner aide.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhide era Wang Silu, military commissioner of Hedong, took him on as staff planner. He rose through posts as rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review, investigating and palace censor, and military commissioner aide.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，入為金部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying he entered the capital as vice director in the Bureau of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying he was recalled to the capital as vice director in the Bureau of the Treasury.

sentences.zh: 尋授侍御史、迥紇糧料使，改檢校職方員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed attendant censor and commissioner for Uyghur grain supplies, then changed to acting vice director in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made attendant censor and commissioner for Uyghur grain supplies, then acting vice director in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 充使檢校郎官，自少遊始也。

translations.literal: Serving as envoy with acting court rank began with Shaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of appointing envoys with acting court rank began with Shaoyou.

sentences.zh: 明年，仆固懷恩奏為河北副元帥判官、兵部郎中、兼侍御史。

translations.literal: The next year Pugu Huai'en memorialized that he be made aide to the deputy commander-in-chief of Hebei, director in the Ministry of War, and concurrently attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Pugu Huai'en appointed him aide to the deputy commander-in-chief of Hebei, director in the Ministry of War, and attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 遷晉州刺史，改同州刺史，未視事，又歷晉、鄭二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Jinzhou, then changed to prefect of Tongzhou; before taking office he again passed through the prefectures of Jin and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Jinzhou, then reassigned to Tongzhou before taking office, and later served again as prefect of Jin and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 少遊為理，長於權變，時推幹濟，然厚斂財貨，交結權幸，以是頻獲遷擢。

translations.literal: Shaoyou in governing was skilled at expedient adaptation; his contemporaries praised his practical ability, yet he heavily levied wealth and goods and cultivated connections with the powerful and favored, and thereby frequently gained promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In office Shaoyou was resourceful and adaptable, and men praised his executive talent. Yet he taxed heavily, cultivated the powerful, and so rose rapidly through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 無幾，澤潞節度使李抱玉表為副使、御史中丞、陳鄭二州留後。

translations.literal: Before long Li Baoyu, military commissioner of Zelu, memorialized that he be made deputy commissioner, censor-in-chief, and acting governor of Chen and Zheng prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Baoyu, military commissioner of Zelu, recommended him as deputy commissioner, censor-in-chief, and acting governor of Chen and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 永泰二年，抱玉又奏為隴右行軍司馬，拜檢校左庶子，依前兼中丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongtai Baoyu again memorialized that he be made marching army secretary of Longyou, appointed acting left attendant of the heir apparent, and as before concurrently censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongtai Baoyu had him named marching army secretary of Longyou and acting left attendant of the heir apparent while retaining the post of censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 其年，除桂州刺史、桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: That same year he was appointed prefect of Guizhou and observation commissioner of the Guiguan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was appointed prefect of Guizhou and observation commissioner of the Guiguan circuit.

sentences.zh: 少遊以嶺僥遐遠，欲規求近郡。

translations.literal: Shaoyou regarded the southern mountains as remote and distant and wished to scheme for a nearer prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou found the Lingnan frontier too remote and began scheming for a post nearer the capital.

sentences.zh: 時中官董秀掌樞密用事，少遊乃宿於其裏，候其下直，際晚謁之，從容曰：「七郎家中人數幾何？

translations.literal: At the time the eunuch Dong Xiu controlled the secretariat and wielded power; Shaoyou lodged in his lane, waited until he left duty, and at dusk paid a visit, saying at ease: "Seventh Brother, how many people are there in your household?
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Dong Xiu then controlled the secretariat. Shaoyou lodged in his lane, waited until he left the palace at dusk, and called on him casually: "Seventh Brother, how large is your household?

sentences.zh: 每月所費復幾何？」

translations.literal: How much do you spend each month?"
translations.idiomatic: And what does it cost you each month?"

sentences.zh: 秀曰：「久忝近職，家累甚重，又屬時物騰貴，一月過千餘貫。」

translations.literal: Xiu said: "For long I have been favored with a post near the throne; my household burden is very heavy, and moreover prices are soaring—more than a thousand strings a month."
translations.idiomatic: Xiu replied: "I have long held a post at court, my household is large, and prices are soaring. It costs more than a thousand strings a month."

sentences.zh: 少遊曰：「據此之費，俸錢不足支數日，其餘常須數求外人，方可取濟。

translations.literal: Shaoyou said: "By this expense, salary would not last a few days; the rest must constantly be sought many times from outsiders before one can make ends meet.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou said: "At that rate your salary would not last a few days. You must constantly beg help from outsiders to make ends meet.

sentences.zh: 倘有輸誠供億者，但留心庇覆之，固易為力耳。

translations.literal: If someone offers sincere support and supplies, you need only take care to shelter him—it is indeed easy to exert force.
translations.idiomatic: If someone offers you loyal support and supplies, you need only shelter him—it is an easy thing to do.

sentences.zh: 少遊雖不才，請以一身獨供七郎之費，每歲請獻錢五萬貫。

translations.literal: Though Shaoyou lacks talent, he asks to supply Seventh Brother's expenses alone by himself, offering fifty thousand strings of cash each year.
translations.idiomatic: I am no great man, but I will supply all of Seventh Brother's expenses myself—fifty thousand strings of cash each year.

sentences.zh: 今見有大半，請即受納，餘到官續送。

translations.literal: More than half is now at hand; please accept it at once, and the remainder will be sent continuously after I take office.
translations.idiomatic: I have more than half of it here now—please accept it at once. The rest I will send after I reach my post.

sentences.zh: 免貴人勞慮，不亦可乎？」

translations.literal: Would it not also spare a noble person worry and labor?"
translations.idiomatic: Would that not spare you worry as well?"

sentences.zh: 秀既逾於始望，欣愜頗甚，因與之厚相結。

translations.literal: Xiu, having exceeded his first expectations, was greatly pleased and satisfied, and therefore formed a deep bond with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu, delighted beyond his hopes, formed a close bond with him.

sentences.zh: 少遊言訖，泣曰：「南方炎瘴，深愴違辭，但恐不生還再睹顏色矣。」

translations.literal: When Shaoyou had finished speaking he wept and said: "The southern heat and miasma deeply grieve me at parting; I fear I shall not return alive to see your face again."
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished, Shaoyou wept and said: "The southern heat and pestilence grieve me at our parting. I fear I shall never return alive to see you again."

sentences.zh: 秀遽曰：「中丞美才，不當遠官，請從容旬日，冀竭蹇分。」

translations.literal: Xiu hastily said: "Vice Censor, your talent is fine—you should not take a distant post. Please wait at ease for ten days; I hope to exhaust my feeble share of effort."
translations.idiomatic: Xiu said at once: "Your talent is too fine for a distant post. Wait ten days at ease while I do what little I can."

sentences.zh: 時少遊又已納賄於元載子仲武矣。

translations.literal: At that time Shaoyou had also already paid bribes to Yuan Zai's son Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shaoyou had also bribed Yuan Zai's son Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 秀、載內外引薦，數日，拜宣州刺史、宣歙池都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: Xiu and Zai recommended him inside and outside the court; within a few days he was appointed prefect of Xuanzhou and overall training-and-observation commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi.
translations.idiomatic: With recommendations from Xiu within the palace and Zai outside, within days he was made prefect of Xuanzhou and overall military governor of Xuan, She, and Chi.

sentences.zh: 大歷五年，改越州刺史、兼御史大夫、浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dali he was changed to prefect of Yuezhou, concurrently chief censor, and observation commissioner of Eastern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dali he was transferred to prefect of Yuezhou, chief censor, and observation commissioner of Eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 八年遷揚州大都督府長史、淮南節度觀察使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to senior adjutant of the metropolitan prefecture of Yangzhou and military commissioner and observation commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made senior adjutant of Yangzhou and military commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 仍加銀青光祿大夫，封潁川縣開國子。

translations.literal: He was further given the title of Silver-Green Glory Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Baron of Yingchuan county.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted the title of Silver-Green Glory Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Baron of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 所在悉心綏輯，而多以任數為政，好行小惠，胥吏得職，人亦獲安。

translations.literal: Wherever he was he devoted himself to pacification and ordering, yet he largely governed by expedient calculation, liked to grant small favors, clerks fulfilled their duties, and the people also found security.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he worked to restore order, though he governed chiefly by calculation and small favors. His clerks did their jobs and the people found a measure of peace.

sentences.zh: 及朝廷多事。

translations.literal: When the court had many affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was beset by troubles,

sentences.zh: 奏請本道兩稅錢千增二百。

translations.literal: he memorialized that the circuit's two-tax cash per thousand be increased by two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: he memorialized to raise the circuit's two-tax levy by two hundred cash per thousand.

sentences.zh: 因詔諸道悉如淮南，鹽每一斗更加一百文。

translations.literal: An edict thereupon ordered all circuits to follow Huainan, adding one hundred cash to each dou of salt.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered every circuit to follow Huainan's example, adding one hundred cash to the price of each dou of salt.

sentences.zh: 少遊十餘年間，三總大籓，皆天下殷厚處也。

translations.literal: Within more than ten years Shaoyou thrice headed great frontier commands, all among the richest places in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than ten years Shaoyou held three of the empire's wealthiest great commands in succession.

sentences.zh: 以故征求貿易，且無虛日，斂積財寶，累巨億萬，多賂遺權貴，視文雅清流之士，蔑如也。

translations.literal: Therefore he levied and traded without a single idle day, amassed treasure amounting to hundreds of millions, gave many bribes to the powerful and noble, and looked down on refined, pure-stream scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He taxed and traded without a day's pause, amassed hundreds of millions in wealth, lavished bribes on the powerful, and held refined scholars in contempt.

sentences.zh: 初結元載，每年饋金帛約十萬貫，又多納賂於用事中官駱奉先、劉清潭、吳承倩等，由是美聲達於中禁。

translations.literal: At first he cultivated Yuan Zai, sending him gold and silks of about one hundred thousand strings each year, and also paid many bribes to influential eunuchs Luo Fengxian, Liu Qingtan, Wu Chengqian, and others; thereby his fine reputation reached the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: He first cultivated Yuan Zai with annual gifts of gold and silk worth some one hundred thousand strings, and bribed influential eunuchs such as Luo Fengxian, Liu Qingtan, and Wu Chengqian until his praise reached the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 後見元載在相位年深，以過犯漸見疑忌，少遊亦稍疏之。

translations.literal: Later, seeing that Yuan Zai had long been in the chief ministership and was gradually suspected for his faults, Shaoyou also grew somewhat distant from him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Yuan Zai's long tenure bred suspicion of his misdeeds, Shaoyou drew somewhat apart from him.

sentences.zh: 無何，載子伯和貶官揚州，少遊外與之交結，而陰使人伺其過失，密以上聞。

translations.literal: Before long Zai's son Bohe was demoted to an office in Yangzhou; Shaoyou outwardly formed ties with him while secretly sending men to watch for his faults and secretly reporting them above.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zai's son Bohe was demoted to Yangzhou. Shaoyou befriended him openly while secretly having his faults reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 代宗以為忠，待之益厚。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong regarded this as loyalty and treated him all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong took this for loyalty and treated him all the more favorably.

sentences.zh: 上即位，累加檢校禮部、兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Shaoyou was repeatedly given the additional titles of acting minister of rites and minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong came to the throne, Shaoyou was repeatedly promoted to acting minister of rites and minister of war.

sentences.zh: 建中三年，李納反叛，少遊以師收徐、海等州，尋棄之，退軍盱眙。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong, when Li Na rebelled, Shaoyou with his army recovered Xu, Hai, and other prefectures, then soon abandoned them and withdrew his army to Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianzhong, when Li Na rebelled, Shaoyou recovered Xu, Hai, and other prefectures, then abandoned them and withdrew to Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 又加檢校左僕射，賜實封三百戶。

translations.literal: He was further made acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and granted three hundred actual fief households.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and granted three hundred actual fief households.

sentences.zh: 其年，就加同平章事。

translations.literal: That same year he was given the additional title of co-chief minister on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made co-chief minister on the spot.

sentences.zh: 關播嘗為少遊賓僚，盧杞早年與之同在仆固懷恩使府，故驟加其官秩。

translations.literal: Guan Bo had once been Shaoyou's staff officer; Lu Qi in his early years had been with him in Pugu Huai'en's mission office—therefore his rank was suddenly raised.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo had once served on his staff, and Lu Qi had been with him in Pugu Huai'en's mission office in their youth—hence his sudden elevation in rank.

sentences.zh: 四年十月，駕幸奉天，度支汴東兩稅使包佶在揚州，尚未知也。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year the emperor went to Fengtian; Bao Ji, commissioner of the two taxes for Bian and the east under the Department of Revenue, was in Yangzhou and did not yet know of it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year the emperor fled to Fengtian. Bao Ji, commissioner of the two taxes for Bian and the east, was in Yangzhou and had not yet heard the news.

sentences.zh: 佶判官崔沅遽報少遊，佶時所總賦稅錢帛約八百萬貫在焉，少遊意以為賊據京師，未即收復，遂脅取其財物。

translations.literal: Ji's aide Cui Yuan hastily reported to Shaoyou; the tax money and silks under Ji's control amounted to about eight million strings; Shaoyou thought the rebels held the capital and it would not soon be recovered, and therefore coerced and seized his goods.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's aide Cui Yuan rushed word to Shaoyou. Bao Ji had some eight million strings in tax revenues on hand. Believing the rebels would hold the capital for some time, Shaoyou seized the funds by force.

sentences.zh: 先使判官崔就佶強索其納給文歷，並請供二百萬貫錢物以助軍費，佶答曰：「所用財帛，須承敕命。」

translations.literal: He first sent his aide Cui to Ji to forcibly demand his payment records and also requested two million strings of money and goods to aid military expenses; Ji replied: "Funds and silks used must await imperial order."
translations.idiomatic: He sent his aide Cui to demand Bao Ji's payment records and two million strings for military expenses. Ji replied: "These funds require an imperial order."

sentences.zh: 未與之。

translations.literal: He would not give them.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 勃然曰：「中丞若得，為劉長卿；

translations.literal: He said angrily: "If the Vice Censor obtains them, he will be like Liu Changqing;
translations.idiomatic: Cui said angrily: "If you get your way, you will be like Liu Changqing;

sentences.zh: 不爾，為崔眾矣。」

translations.literal: if not, like Cui Zhong."
translations.idiomatic: if not, like Cui Zhong."

sentences.zh: 長卿嘗任租庸使，為吳仲孺所困，崔眾供軍吝財，為光弼所殺，故言及之，佶大懼，不敢固護，財帛將轉輸入京師者，悉為少遊奪之。

translations.literal: Changqing had once served as transport commissioner and was trapped by Wu Zhongru; Cui Zhong was stingy with army funds and was killed by Li Guangbi—hence he mentioned them. Ji was greatly afraid and did not dare firmly protect the goods; all money and silks about to be transported to the capital were seized by Shaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changqing had once been transport commissioner and was ruined by Wu Zhongru; Cui Zhong had hoarded army funds and was executed by Li Guangbi. Ji was terrified and did not resist. All funds bound for the capital were seized by Shaoyou.

sentences.zh: 佶自謁，少遊止焉，長揖而遣，既懼禍，奔往白沙。

translations.literal: Ji went in person to call on him; Shaoyou stopped him, gave a long bow and sent him away; fearing disaster, Ji fled to Baisha.
translations.idiomatic: Ji came to call on him in person. Shaoyou received him with a formal bow and dismissed him. Fearing for his life, Ji fled to Baisha.

sentences.zh: 少遊又遣判官房孺復召之，佶愈懼，托以巡檢，因急棹過江，妻子伏案牘中。

translations.literal: Shaoyou again sent his aide Fang Rufu to summon him; Ji grew still more afraid, pleaded an inspection tour, and urgently rowed across the river, his wife and children hiding among the documents.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou sent his aide Fang Rufu to summon him again. Ji, more frightened still, claimed an inspection tour and rowed hastily across the river, his wife and children hidden among the document cases.

sentences.zh: 至上元，復為韓滉所拘留。

translations.literal: When he reached Shangyuan he was again detained by Han Huang.
translations.idiomatic: At Shangyuan he was detained again by Han Huang.

sentences.zh: 佶先有兵三千，守禦財貨，令高越、元甫將焉，少遊盡奪之。

translations.literal: Ji had previously had three thousand troops guarding the treasure, commanded by Gao Yue and Yuan Fu; Shaoyou seized them all.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had left three thousand troops under Gao Yue and Yuan Fu to guard the treasure; Shaoyou seized them all.

sentences.zh: 隨佶渡江者，又為韓滉所留，佶但領胥吏往江、鄂等州。

translations.literal: Those who crossed the river with Ji were again held by Han Huang; Ji led only clerks on to Jiang, E, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Those who crossed the river with Ji were detained by Han Huang as well, and Ji went on to Jiang, E, and other prefectures with only a few clerks.

sentences.zh: 佶於彈丸中置表，以少遊脅取財帛事。

translations.literal: Ji placed a memorial inside a pellet, reporting Shaoyou's coercion of money and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Ji hid a memorial inside a pellet, reporting Shaoyou's seizure of the funds.

sentences.zh: 會少遊使繼至，上問曰：「少遊取包佶財帛，有之乎？」

translations.literal: When Shaoyou's envoy next arrived, the emperor asked: "Did Shaoyou take Bao Ji's money and silks—is it so?"
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyou's envoy next arrived, the emperor asked: "Did Shaoyou seize Bao Ji's funds—is that true?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣發揚州後，非所知也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "After your servant left Yangzhou, it was not known to him."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "After I left Yangzhou, I did not know."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「少遊國之守臣，或防他盜，供費軍旅，收亦何傷。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Shaoyou is a guardian minister of the state; perhaps guarding against other robbers and supplying the army—what harm in taking it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Shaoyou is a guardian of the realm. If he took the funds to guard against other thieves or supply the army, what harm was there?"

sentences.zh: 時方隅阻絕，國命未振，遠近聞之大驚，鹹以聖情達於變通，明見萬里。

translations.literal: At that time the regions were cut off and the nation's mandate had not revived; near and far heard this and were greatly astonished, all considering that the sage heart reached expedient adaptation and saw clearly for ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The regions were cut off and the dynasty still reeling. Near and far, men marveled that the emperor's judgment reached so far and adapted so wisely to circumstance.

sentences.zh: 少遊後聞之，乃安。

translations.literal: When Shaoyou later heard of it he was reassured.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyou later heard of this he was reassured.

sentences.zh: 及李希烈陷汴州，聲言欲襲江淮。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie captured Bianzhou he declared he would strike the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie captured Bianzhou he announced his intention to strike the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 少遊懼，乃使參謀溫述由壽州送款於希烈曰：「濠、壽、舒、廬，尋令罷壘，韜戈卷甲，佇候指揮。」

translations.literal: Shaoyou was afraid and sent his staff planner Wen Shu from Shouzhou to offer submission to Xilie, saying: "Hao, Shou, Shu, and Lu—soon I shall order the forts dismantled, weapons sheathed and armor rolled up, awaiting your command."
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Shaoyou sent his staff planner Wen Shu from Shouzhou to offer submission to Xilie: "At Hao, Shou, Shu, and Lu I shall soon dismantle the forts, sheathe our weapons, and await your orders."

sentences.zh: 少遊又遣巡官趙詵於鄆州結李納。

translations.literal: Shaoyou also sent touring officer Zhao Shen to Yanzhou to ally with Li Na.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou also sent touring officer Zhao Shen to Yanzhou to ally with Li Na.

sentences.zh: 其年，希烈僭號，遣其將楊豐賫偽赦書赴揚州，至壽州，為刺史張建封候騎所得，建封對中使二人及少遊判官許子瑞廷責豐而斬之。

translations.literal: That year Xilie usurped the title of emperor and sent his general Yang Feng bearing a false amnesty to Yangzhou; at Shouzhou he was seized by Prefect Zhang Jianfeng's scouting horsemen; Jianfeng, in the presence of two palace envoys and Shaoyou's aide Xu Zirui, rebuked Feng in court and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xilie declared himself emperor and sent his general Yang Feng with a false amnesty to Yangzhou. At Shouzhou, Prefect Zhang Jianfeng's scouts seized him. Before two palace envoys and Shaoyou's aide Xu Zirui, Jianfeng rebuked Feng publicly and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 希烈聞之大怒，即署其大將杜少誠為偽僕射、淮南節度，令先平壽州，後取廣陵。

translations.literal: Xilie heard this and was greatly enraged; he immediately appointed his great general Du Shaoqian false vice director and military commissioner of Huainan, ordering him first to pacify Shouzhou and then take Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie was furious and appointed his general Du Shaoqian false vice director and military commissioner of Huainan, ordering him first to take Shouzhou and then Guangling.

sentences.zh: 建封於霍丘堅柵，嚴加守禁，少誠竟不能進。

translations.literal: Jianfeng built strong palisades at Huoqiu and strictly enforced guard prohibitions; Shaoqian in the end could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng fortified Huoqiu and held it strictly. Shaoqian could not break through.

sentences.zh: 後包佶入朝，具奏少遊奪財賦事狀，少遊大懼，乃上表，以所取包佶財貨，皆是供軍急用，今請據數卻納。

translations.literal: Later, when Bao Ji entered court and fully reported the circumstances of Shaoyou's seizure of revenues, Shaoyou was greatly afraid and submitted a memorial stating that the goods taken from Bao Ji had all been urgently used to supply the army, and he now asked to return them according to the amount.
translations.idiomatic: Later Bao Ji reached court and reported the seizure in full. Shaoyou was terrified and memorialized that the funds had all been spent on urgent military needs and that he would repay the full amount.

sentences.zh: 既而州府殘破，無以上填，乃與腹心孔目官等設法重稅管內百姓以供之。

translations.literal: Soon the prefecture and offices were ravaged and there was no way to make repayment upward; he therefore joined with trusted ledger clerks and others to devise methods of heavy taxation on the people within his jurisdiction to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: But his jurisdiction lay in ruins and he could not repay the throne. He and his trusted clerks therefore imposed heavy new taxes on the people to raise the sum.

sentences.zh: 無何，劉洽收汴州，得希烈偽起居註「某月日陳少遊上表歸順。」

translations.literal: Before long Liu Qia recovered Bianzhou and obtained Xilie's false diary of attendance: "On such-and-such a month and day Chen Shaoyou submitted a memorial of submission."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liu Qia recovered Bianzhou and found among Xilie's papers a false court diary entry: "On such-and-such a day Chen Shaoyou submitted a memorial of submission."

sentences.zh: 少遊聞之，慚惶發疾，數日而卒，年六十一，贈太尉，賻布帛，葬祭如常儀。

translations.literal: When Shaoyou heard of it he was ashamed and alarmed, fell ill, and died within several days at the age of sixty-one; he was posthumously honored as Grand Marshal, given funeral silks, and buried and sacrificed to with the usual rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyou heard this he was stricken with shame and alarm, fell ill, and died within days, aged sixty-one. He was posthumously honored as Grand Marshal, and buried with the usual state rites.

sentences.zh: 盧鸑，幽州范陽人也，貞觀中工部侍郎義恭玄孫也。

translations.literal: Lu Yue was a man of Fanyang in Youzhou, the great-great-grandson of Yigong, vice minister of works in the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yue was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou and the great-great-grandson of Yigong, vice minister of works under Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 父子騫，潁王府諮議參軍，以鸑贈秘書少監。

translations.literal: His father Ziqian was advisory staff officer of the Prince of Ying's establishment; through Yue he was posthumously honored as vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ziqian had been advisory staff officer in the Prince of Ying's household and was posthumously honored as vice director of the Secretariat through Yue's promotions.

sentences.zh: 鸑少以門廕入仕，在職以幹局稱。

translations.literal: Yue in youth entered office by yin privilege and in service was known for practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: Yue entered office young through hereditary privilege and was known in service for practical competence.

sentences.zh: 累授閬州錄事參軍、監察殿中御史、侍御史、金州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed recorder of Langzhou, investigating censor and palace censor, attendant censor, and prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts as recorder of Langzhou, investigating and palace censor, attendant censor, and prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 宰相楊炎遇之頗厚，召入左司郎中、京兆少尹，遷大尹。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Yang Yan treated him quite generously, summoned him in as director in the Left Secretariat and junior metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, then promoted him to metropolitan governor.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Yang Yan favored him, recalled him as director in the Left Secretariat and junior metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, then promoted him to metropolitan governor.

sentences.zh: 鸑無術學，善事權要，為政苛躁。

translations.literal: Yue had no learning in the arts, was good at serving the powerful, and in governing was harsh and impatient.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had no scholarly training, cultivated the powerful, and governed with harsh impatience.

sentences.zh: 盧杞甚惡之，諷有司彈奏，坐貶撫州司馬同正，改饒州刺史，遷福州刺史、福建觀察使。

translations.literal: Lu Qi greatly hated him, prompted the relevant offices to impeach him, and he was demoted to secretary of Fuzhou with the same nominal rank, then changed to prefect of Raozhou, and transferred to prefect of Fuzhou and observation commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi detested him, had him impeached, and demoted him to secretary of Fuzhou. He was later made prefect of Raozhou, then of Fuzhou and observation commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年七月，以疾終。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Zhenyuan he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the seventh month of the second year of Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 裴谞，字士明，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Pei Xu, courtesy name Shiming, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xu, whose courtesy name was Shiming, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父寬，禮部尚書，有重名於開元、天寶間。

translations.literal: His father Kuan was minister of rites and had a great reputation in the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuan had served as minister of rites and enjoyed great renown in the Kaiyuan and Tianbao reigns.

sentences.zh: 谞少舉明經，補河南府參軍，通達簡率，不好苛細。

translations.literal: Xu in youth passed the mingjing examination, was appointed staff officer of Henan prefecture, was open and direct in manner, and disliked petty detail.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Xu passed the mingjing examination and served as staff officer of Henan prefecture. He was open and direct by nature and disliked petty detail.

sentences.zh: 積官至京兆倉曹，丁父喪，居東都。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to granary clerk of Jingzhao, entered mourning for his father, and resided in the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to granary clerk of Jingzhao, then retired to the eastern capital to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 是時，安祿山盜陷二京，東都收復，遷太子司議郎。

translations.literal: At that time An Lushan rebelliously seized the two capitals; when the eastern capital was recovered, Xu was transferred to gentleman for deliberation of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan seized the two capitals and the eastern capital was later recovered, Xu was appointed gentleman for deliberation of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 無幾，虢王巨奏署侍御史、襄鄧營田判官，丁母憂。

translations.literal: Before long the Prince of Guo, Ju, memorialized that he be appointed attendant censor and aide for garrison fields of Xiang and Deng; he then entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Prince of Guo had him appointed attendant censor and aide for the garrison fields of Xiang and Deng. He then entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 東都復為史思明所陷，谞藏匿山谷。

translations.literal: The eastern capital was again seized by Shi Siming, and Xu hid in the mountains and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern capital fell again to Shi Siming, Xu hid in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 思明嘗為谞父將校，懷舊恩，又素慕谞名，欲必得之，因令捕騎數十跡逐得谞。

translations.literal: Siming had once been a commander under Xu's father, cherished the old favor, and had long admired Xu's name; wishing to obtain him at all costs, he sent several dozen mounted pursuers who tracked him down and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Siming had once served under Xu's father and, cherishing that old tie and long admiring Xu's reputation, was determined to have him. He sent dozens of mounted pursuers who tracked Xu down and captured him.

sentences.zh: 思明見之，甚喜，呼為郎君，不名，偽授御史中丞，主擊斷。

translations.literal: When Siming saw him he was greatly pleased, called him Young Master without using his name, falsely appointed him censor-in-chief, and put him in charge of judicial decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Siming was delighted, addressed him as Young Master without using his name, and falsely appointed him censor-in-chief in charge of judicial decisions.

sentences.zh: 時思明殘殺宗室，谞陰緩之，全活者數百人。

translations.literal: At that time Siming slaughtered members of the imperial clan; Xu secretly slowed the process, and several hundred were preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: As Siming slaughtered members of the imperial clan, Xu secretly slowed the process and saved several hundred lives.

sentences.zh: 又嘗疏賊短長以聞，事泄，思明大怒詬罵，僅而免死。

translations.literal: He also once memorialized the rebels' strengths and weaknesses to inform the court; when the matter leaked out Siming raged and reviled him, and he barely escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent intelligence on the rebels' strengths and weaknesses to the court. When this was discovered, Siming raged at him and he barely escaped execution.

sentences.zh: 賊平，除太子中允，遷考功郎中，數召見言事。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was appointed gentleman attendant of the heir apparent, promoted to director in the Bureau of Evaluations, and repeatedly summoned to audience to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed he was made gentleman attendant of the heir apparent, then director in the Bureau of Evaluations, and was repeatedly summoned to advise the throne.

sentences.zh: 代宗居陜，谞步懷考功及南曹二印赴行在，上見而謂之曰：「疾風知勁草，果信矣。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong was in Shaan, Xu walked on foot carrying the seals of the Bureau of Evaluations and the Southern Bureau to the mobile court; when the emperor saw him he said: "A fierce wind reveals the tough grass—how true indeed."
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong was at Shaan, Xu walked on foot to the mobile court carrying the seals of the Bureau of Evaluations and the Southern Bureau. The emperor said: "A fierce wind reveals the tough grass—how true that proves."

sentences.zh: 將以為御史中丞，為無載所排，為河東道租庸鹽鐵等使。

translations.literal: He was about to be made censor-in-chief but was blocked by Yuan Zai and instead made commissioner of transport, salt, and iron for the Hedong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was to be made censor-in-chief, but Yuan Zai blocked the appointment and he was made commissioner of transport, salt, and iron for Hedong instead.

sentences.zh: 時關輔大旱，谞入計，代宗召見便殿，問谞：「榷酤之利，一歲出入幾何？」

translations.literal: At that time the Guanzhong region suffered great drought; when Xu came to present accounts, Daizong summoned him in the side hall and asked Xu: "What are the yearly receipts and expenditures of the monopoly on wine?"
translations.idiomatic: A great drought afflicted the Guanzhong region. When Xu came to present accounts, Daizong received him in the side hall and asked: "What are the yearly receipts and expenditures of the wine monopoly?"

sentences.zh: 谞久之不對。

translations.literal: Xu for a long time did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was silent for a long time.

sentences.zh: 上復問之，對曰：「臣有所思。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked again, and he replied: "Your servant has something on his mind."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again. Xu replied: "I have been thinking."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「何思？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What are you thinking?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "About what?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣自河東來，其間所歷三百里，見農人愁嘆，谷菽未種。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant has come from Hedong; over three hundred li along the way I saw farmers sighing in grief, grain and beans not yet sown.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Coming from Hedong I traveled three hundred li and saw farmers grieving—grain and beans still unplanted.

sentences.zh: 誠謂陛下軫念，先問人之疾苦，而乃責臣以利。

translations.literal: I truly thought Your Majesty would be concerned and first ask about the people's hardship, yet you charge your servant about profit.
translations.idiomatic: I had hoped Your Majesty would first ask about the people's hardship, yet you question me about profit.

sentences.zh: 孟子曰：理國者，仁義而已，何以利為？

translations.literal: Mencius said: To order a state is nothing but benevolence and righteousness—why speak of profit?
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said that to govern a state is nothing but benevolence and righteousness—why speak of profit?

sentences.zh: 由是未敢即對也。」

translations.literal: For this reason I did not dare answer at once."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I did not answer at once."

sentences.zh: 上前坐曰：「微公言，吾不聞此。」

translations.literal: The emperor rose and sat forward and said: "But for your words I would not have heard this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor leaned forward and said: "Without your words I would never have heard this."

sentences.zh: 拜左司郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed director in the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was appointed director in the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上時訪以事，執政者忌之，出為虔州刺史，歷饒、廬、亳三州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor often consulted him on affairs; those in power envied him and he was sent out as prefect of Qianzhou, then served as prefect of Rao, Lu, and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often consulted him, but those in power envied him and he was sent out as prefect of Qianzhou, then served successively at Rao, Lu, and Bo.

sentences.zh: 入為右金吾將軍。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as general of the Right Gold Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as general of the Right Gold Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 建中初，上以刑名理天下，百吏震悚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong the emperor governed the realm by penal law, and all officials were shaken and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong era the emperor governed through penal law, and every official trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 時十月禁屠殺，以甫近山陵，禁益嚴。

translations.literal: At that time slaughter was forbidden in the tenth month; because it was near the imperial tombs the prohibition was especially strict.
translations.idiomatic: Slaughter was forbidden in the tenth month, and as the season drew near the imperial tombs the ban grew especially strict.

sentences.zh: 尚父、汾陽王郭子儀隸人殺羊以入，門者覺之，谞列奏狀，上以為不畏強禦，累遣宣諭。

translations.literal: The Esteemed Father, Prince of Fenyang Guo Ziyi, had a servant slaughter a sheep and bring it in; the gate guards detected it; Xu submitted a detailed memorial; the emperor considered that he did not fear the powerful and repeatedly sent imperial commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The Esteemed Father, Guo Ziyi, Prince of Fenyang, had a servant slaughter a sheep and bring it in. The gate guards caught him, and Xu memorialized the offense. The emperor praised his fearlessness before the powerful and repeatedly commended him.

sentences.zh: 或謂谞曰：「郭公有社稷功，豈不為蓋之？」

translations.literal: Someone said to Xu: "The Duke has merit for the altars of state—would you not cover this for him?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked him: "The Duke has saved the dynasty—would you not cover this for him?"

sentences.zh: 谞笑曰：「非爾所解。

translations.literal: Xu smiled and said: "This is not something you would understand.
translations.idiomatic: Xu smiled and said: "That is not something you would understand.

sentences.zh: 且郭公威權太盛，上新即位，必謂黨附者眾。

translations.literal: Moreover the Duke's authority and power are too great; the emperor has newly taken the throne and is sure to think that those who attach themselves to him are many.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke's power is too great. The new emperor is sure to suspect that his following is too large.

sentences.zh: 今發其細過，以明不弄權耳。

translations.literal: Now by exposing his small fault I make clear that I do not play with power.
translations.idiomatic: By exposing this small fault I show that I do not court his power.

sentences.zh: 吾上以盡事君之道，下以安大臣，不亦可乎？」

translations.literal: Above I thereby fulfill the way of serving the ruler; below I thereby reassure a great minister—is that not acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Above, I fulfill my duty to the ruler; below, I reassure a great minister. Is that not fitting?"

sentences.zh: 時於朝堂別置三司以決庶獄，辯爭者輒擊登聞鼓，谞上疏曰：「夫諫豉謗木之設，所以達幽枉，延直言。

translations.literal: At that time three offices were separately established in the court hall to decide common cases; those in dispute would strike the Petition Drum; Xu submitted a memorial saying: "The setting up of the admonition drum and the slander post was to reach hidden wrongs and extend straight speech.
translations.idiomatic: Separate tribunals had been set up in the court hall to decide common cases, and litigants would strike the Petition Drum. Xu memorialized: "The admonition drum and the slander post were established to reach hidden wrongs and give voice to honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 今輕猾之人，援桴鳴鼓，始動天聽，竟因纖微。

translations.literal: Now frivolous and cunning men take the mallet and sound the drum, first moving heaven's hearing, yet in the end it is over trifles.
translations.idiomatic: Now frivolous and cunning men beat the drum, reach the emperor's ear, and in the end it is over trifles.

sentences.zh: 若然者，安用吏理乎！」

translations.literal: If it is thus, what use are officials and governance!"
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, what need is there for officials and regular governance!"

sentences.zh: 上然之，悉歸有司。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this and returned all cases to the regular offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and returned all such cases to the regular courts.

sentences.zh: 谞以法吏舞文，多挾宿怨，因獻《獄官箴》以諷。

translations.literal: Xu considered that legal clerks twisted the written law and often carried old grudges; he therefore presented the "Admonition for Prison Officials" as a satire.
translations.idiomatic: Believing that legal clerks twisted the law and often pursued old grudges, Xu presented his "Admonition for Prison Officials" as an indirect critique.

sentences.zh: 無何，坐所善僧抵法，貶閬州司馬。

translations.literal: Before long, because a monk he favored violated the law, he was demoted to secretary of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was demoted to secretary of Langzhou because a monk he favored had broken the law.

sentences.zh: 征為右庶子，改千牛上將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as right attendant of the heir apparent, then changed to general of the Palace Domestic Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as right attendant of the heir apparent, then made general of the Palace Domestic Army.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃入寇，尋拜吏部侍郎、兼御史大夫，為吐蕃使，不行。

translations.literal: When Tibet invaded he was soon appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently chief censor, and was made envoy to Tibet but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet invaded he was soon made vice minister of personnel and chief censor and appointed envoy to Tibet, but did not go.

sentences.zh: 無幾，轉太子賓客、兵部侍郎、河南尹、東都副留守。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to guest of the heir apparent, vice minister of war, metropolitan governor of Henan, and deputy protector of the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he became guest of the heir apparent, vice minister of war, metropolitan governor of Henan, and deputy protector of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 谞自河南凡五代為官，入視事，未嘗當正處，不鞫認於贓罪，以寬厚和易為理。

translations.literal: Xu's family had served as officials in Henan for five generations; when he entered to conduct affairs he never sat in the main seat, did not press confessions in cases of embezzlement, and governed with generous forbearance and mild ease.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations of Xu's family had served in Henan. When he took office he never sat in the chief seat, did not press confessions in corruption cases, and governed with generous mildness.

sentences.zh: 貞元九年十一月，以疾終，年七十五，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the ninth year of Zhenyuan he died of illness at the age of seventy-five and was posthumously honored as minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the eleventh month of the ninth year of Zhenyuan, aged seventy-five, and was posthumously honored as minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：李揆發言沃心，幸遇明主；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Li Kui's words enriched the imperial heart, and he was fortunate to meet an enlightened ruler;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Li Kui's counsel enriched the emperor's mind, and he was fortunate to serve an enlightened ruler;

sentences.zh: 蔽賢固位，終非令人。

translations.literal: yet in screening the worthy and holding fast to office he was in the end not a man to be approved.
translations.idiomatic: yet in blocking the worthy to hold his post he proved in the end no admirable man.

sentences.zh: 少遊逐勢利隨時，盧惎事權要巧宦，察言觀行，皆無可稱。

translations.literal: Shaoyou chased profit and power as times changed; Lu Yue served the powerful in crafty office-seeking—examining their words and observing their conduct, none is praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou chased profit with the times; Lu Yue curried favor with the powerful through crafty office-seeking. Judging their words and conduct, none deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 涵節行著聞，谞和易為理，庶幾近仁也。

translations.literal: Han was renowned for his restraint and conduct; Xu governed with mild ease—they nearly approached benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Han was renowned for restraint and integrity; Xu governed with mild ease. Both nearly approached true benevolence.

sentences.zh: 贊曰李、陳、盧鸑，言行非真。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Li, Chen, and Lu Yue—their words and conduct were not true.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Li, Chen, and Lu Yue—their words and conduct were not genuine.

sentences.zh: 涵、谞和易，庶乎近仁。

translations.literal: Han and Xu were mild and easy—they nearly approached benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Xu were mild in manner—they nearly approached true benevolence.
